match.reason: No bank point covers both the types of evidence (facts, statistics, expert opinion, examples) and placing the strongest evidence to give a text authority, so the closest cards are only partial matches and the NSW point needs its own card.

draft.title: Evidence and authority
card: a statement that can be checked and shown to be true. Example: the school library has 12 000 books.
a number that measures something. Example: 8 out of 10 students walk to school.
a view from a person with real knowledge of the topic, such as a doctor talking about sleep. An example is a real case that shows the point in action.

Evidence gives a text authority when it comes from a reliable source, one that is accurate and in a position to know. The strongest evidence often goes where it has most impact, such as early to win attention or last to leave a strong final impression.
draft.remember: Good evidence from a reliable source makes a writer believable.

a.q: Which sentence uses a statistic to support an argument?
opts: Nine out of ten Year 7 students sleep under eight hours
Many Year 7 students seem to be tired in class
Sleep is something that every young person needs
Our school should start later so students feel rested
a.why: A statistic is a number that measures something, and nine out of ten does that. The sentence about many students being tired is a general claim with no measurement, so it is not a statistic.
a.clue: Look for the option that measures something with a number.

b.q: Jaya argues that her town needs a new skate park. Which source would give her argument the most authority?
opts: A council report counting injuries at current ramps
A post from a stranger saying skate parks are great
Her own feeling that skating is more fun than football
A rumour that another town built one last year
b.why: A council report is a reliable source in a position to know, and it gives facts and numbers that can be checked. A stranger's post is only an unsupported opinion, so it is tempting but weak.
b.clue: Which source can be checked and is in a position to know?

a.best: Nine out of ten Year 7 students sleep under eight hours

b.best: A council report counting injuries at current ramps

problems.detail: The definition of an example ('An example is a real case that shows the point in action') sits inside the Expert opinion bullet. A student could read it as part of what expert opinion means. It should be its own bullet.

proposal.title: Evidence and authority
card: Evidence is what backs up an argument. A fact is a statement that can be checked and shown to be true, such as Canberra being the capital of Australia.

A statistic is a number that measures something, such as 8 out of 10 students walking to school. Expert opinion is a view from someone with real knowledge of the topic, such as a doctor talking about sleep.
An example is a real case that shows the point in action, such as one student whose marks rose after more sleep.

Evidence gives a text authority when it comes from a reliable source, one that is accurate and in a position to know. The strongest evidence often goes early to win attention or last to leave a strong final impression.
proposal.remember: Good evidence from a reliable source makes a writer believable.
